definitions.item_scores: d = c - x and q = (c - x)^2 per tagged response, c = LEVELS[round(Confidence/25)] in {0,.25,.5,.75,1}, x = IsCorrect; bias = mean(d), Brier = mean(q)
definitions.design: Design A pool (>= 200 tagged responses); same N-subsamples as the submitted curves (default_rng([42, 5, N, sid]), sid 1 = S1/t12, 2 = S2/t34)
definitions.split_half_sb: mean over 50 random per-student splits of the Spearman-Brown corrected Pearson r (reliability.py), recomputed here on the same generator and equal to the baseline curves (gate G1)
definitions.icc1_N: one-way random-effects ICC(1,N) = (MSB - MSW) / MSB on the n x N subsample matrix; = G coefficient of an r:p (responses nested in persons) design; equals sigma_p^2 / (sigma_p^2 + sigma_e^2 / N)
definitions.sigma_p2: person variance (MSB - MSW) / N (per-N) or var(m_i) - mean(s_i^2 / n_i) (all responses of each pool student, unweighted moment estimator, as in the paper's EB model)
definitions.sigma_e2: within-person residual variance of the item-level score (MSW per-N; mean s_i^2 for all responses)
definitions.implied_n: n*(t) = t / (1 - t) * sigma_e^2 / sigma_p^2, the volume at which sigma_p^2 / (sigma_p^2 + sigma_e^2 / n) = t
definitions.icc_curve_minN: crossing of the ICC(1,N) grid curve with the same rule as the paper (first crossing, linear in log N); CI from a joint student bootstrap over the grid (B = 1000, default_rng([42, 101, sid]))
definitions.sem_split: SD of observed full-N bias across pool students x sqrt(1 - split-half SB)
definitions.sem_vc: sqrt(MSW / N) = SD_obs x sqrt(1 - ICC(1,N)) exactly
definitions.median_ci_halfwidth: median over pool students of 1.96 x s_i / sqrt(N), s_i = within-student SD of d on the N-subsample (ddof 1)
definitions.points: SEM tables are in confidence-scale points (x 100; bias of 0.10 = 10 points)
definitions.alpha_subset: S2 quizzes: students who rated EVERY question of the quiz (selected subset); complete crossed students x items matrix; QuizId -1 excluded; >= 100 complete students and >= 4 items (primary set >= 300)
definitions.alpha: Cronbach alpha on item-level d (bias) or q (Brier); self-checked equal to two-way ICC(C,k) and to the mean Flanagan-Rulon coefficient over all equal splits (even k <= 14)
definitions.phi: G-theory absolute coefficient for the crossed p x i design, item main effect counted as error
definitions.icc1_k: one-way ICC(1,k) on the quiz matrix, items treated as nested (item variance in error)
definitions.sb_per_student: the paper's estimator on the quiz matrix: per-student random partitions (reliability.half_indices), 50 splits
definitions.sb_common: one common random item partition for all students, 50 partitions, mean SB
definitions.share_item_var_of_error: sigma_i^2 / (sigma_i^2 + sigma_pi,e^2) in the crossed G-study
definitions.quiz_student_rows: n_students_total in the alpha summaries = number of (quiz, student) rows summed over quizzes; one student can appear in several quizzes, so this is NOT a count of distinct students
definitions.relative_vs_absolute: alpha (= E rho^2) is the coefficient for relative (rank-order) use on a common form; Phi is the coefficient for absolute use (bias against zero, e.g. calling a student overconfident), where item effects do not cancel even on a crossed form

not_computable.gamma_auroc_alpha: Not defined. Gamma and AUROC are pair-count ratios over a student's correct-incorrect pairs, not sums or means of item-level scores, so there is no item-level score whose covariance matrix alpha or a variance-components model could use. Not approximated.
not_computable.gamma_auroc_vc: Not defined for the same reason.
not_computable.s1_alpha: Not computed. No S1 quiz has >= 100 students who rated every item; the largest has 70 students with 5 items (feasibility block). S1 numbers stay out of the manuscript.
not_computable.temporal_split: Not part of stream B: the variance-components model assumes exchangeable responses, which temporal halves violate by design.

auroc_rule_independence: bias and Brier do not use the AUROC/gamma tie rule; every number here is unaffected by stream A.
